newsitem.title: GERMANY: German building strike would be disaster-employers.
newsitem.headline: German building strike would be disaster-employers.

text.p: German construction employers said on Monday they were baffled by a decision by builders' unions to reject an arbitration-brokered pay deal and said strikes would be "catastrophic" for the German construction sector.
"Any subsequent strike would be a catastrophe for the recession-plagued construction industry," the ZDB and the BI, two employers' associations in the building sector, said.

IG Bau said it may resort to strikes to secure 100 percent sick-pay benefits for its workers, rejecting the decision of the arbitration committee for workers to receive 80 percent pay for the first three weeks of sickness.
The cutbacks in sick pay and the Christmas bonus have found particular disfavour with union officials.
The IG Bau union had, among other demands, called for wage increase of 2.9 percent and continued full pay during sick leave, while employers had sought to keep pay unchanged.
Under the proposed deal, workers' pay will be cut by 20 percent during the first three weeks of sickness, wages will be raised by 1.3 percent from last April 1 and Christmas bonuses will also be cut.
The employers' associations said that even in the event of being sick for six weeks, the employee would still have five weeks holiday left under the proposed changes.
The only winners if strike action were to be taken would be other European building groups with cheap labour who would take away badly-needed contracts from German firms, the employers' groups said.
